properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 16 at 1:05PM MDT until September 16 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Lee Fire burn scar in...
South Central Rio Blanco County in northwestern Colorado...

* Until 400 PM MDT.

* At 105 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Lee Fire Burn Scar. Between 0.2 and 0.5 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Lee Fire Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Lee Fire Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Rio Blanco County.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 16 at 10:01AM MDT until September 18 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be
possible.

* WHERE...The Eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of thunderstorms are forecast Wednesday afternoon
through Thursday evening producing periods of heavy rainfall and
potential flash flooding.
- Creede, South Fork and Wolf Creek Pass.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 16 at 9:39AM MDT until September 18 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River,
Northwest San Juan Mountains, San Juan River Basin and Southwest
San Juan Mountains.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
This also includes the Gold Mountain, Elk and Ferris burn scars as
well as areas of steep, susceptible terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Recent heavy rainfall in southwest Colorado has led to already
saturated ground. In addition, multiple rounds of showers and
thunderstorms are expected Wednesday afternoon through Thursday
evening producing periods of heavy rainfall and potential flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Northwestern San Juan Mountains; Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin
